turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’m here for my annual well-check, but I’ve also noticed a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the back of my left hand. It doesn’t hurt and isn’t tender.
How long has this plaque been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size, color, or surface (such as bleeding, crusting, or rapid growth)?
“I first noticed the plaque a few months ago, and I think it’s been slowly getting a bit larger. The color seems about the same—rough and scaly—with no bleeding, crusting, or rapid growth.”
Do you have a history of significant cumulative sun exposure, fair skin, or frequent sunburns?

“I’ve had a lot of time outdoors over the years, and I do enjoy walking and sunbathing, so I get regular sun exposure. I’m not sure about having fair skin or frequent sunburns—I don’t recall significant sunburns.”
When you press on the plaque, does it feel firm or hard underneath, or is it relatively flat and soft?
“It feels firm underneath, not soft—like it’s slightly raised and hard.”
What color is the plaque (e.g., pink, red, brown, or skin-colored)?
“It’s kind of skin-colored to slightly pinkish-brown, not bright red. The surface looks rough and scaly, and it feels firm when I press on it.”
[DDX] Actinic keratosis, Squamous cell carcinoma, Bowen disease, Seborrheic keratosis, Verruca vulgaris
